summary: prosocks installs boot-persistent SOCKS5 proxyware controlled by hardcoded remote panel
details: prosocks 1.0.20 turns the installing host into a proxyware exit node under the control of a hardcoded remote operator at https://kalnetz.store. setup.py's custom install_lib hook writes a prosocks.pth file into site-packages whose code runs on every Python interpreter startup: it creates ~/.prosocks/config.json pointing at https://kalnetz.store and spawns `python -m prosocks https://kalnetz.store` in the background with silenced stdio. prosocks.py additionally invokes _auto_launch() at module top level, so any `import prosocks` triggers the same background subprocess. Once running, ProSocksAgent.start() binds a SOCKS5 server on 0.0.0.0:9050 (all interfaces) with a locally generated password, fetches the host's public IP from api.ipify.org, and POSTs the agent id, proxy port, password, and public IP to https://kalnetz.store/api/register, followed by periodic /api/bandwidth and /api/heartbeat callbacks. All requests set verify=False, disabling TLS validation. The panel URL is hardcoded and not user-configurable. The combined effect of pip-install-time.pth persistence, import-time auto-launch, an unattended world-reachable SOCKS5 listener whose credential is shipped to the operator, and host-identifier exfiltration is a proxyware backdoor that gives the operator the ability to relay arbitrary traffic through the installer's network and host identity.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
